name: Physics-Informed Direct Inverse Operator Learning (PI-DION)
summary: Learn a mapping directly from measurements to unknown PDE coefficients or source terms, with embedded physical constraints.
core_idea: Represent the inverse operator by a network and train it using governing equations without fully labeled inverse pairs.
innovation: Amortizes inverse inference across instances rather than repeatedly solving optimization per observed dataset.
limitations: Ill-posedness and nonidentifiability still limit recovered parameters.
Requires sufficiently informative measurement families and robust physical modeling.

start_here.why: Peer-reviewed example developing inverse operator learning without labeled inverse targets.
start_here.focus: Inverse mapping, physics loss, and stability assumptions before technical proofs.

curation_note: Scholarly source and method contribution checked; starting references are suggestions, not mandatory reading.
